html:
A battle near Varna on the Black Sea coast of Bulgaria on 10 November 1444, where the Ottomans under Murad II destroyed a crusading army.

The crusade came out of the church union agreed at the Council of Florence. Its leaders were Władysław III, king of Poland and of Hungary, and the Hungarian general John Hunyadi. That summer they had signed a truce with Murad, then broke it and marched into Bulgaria. Murad, who had handed the throne to his young son Mehmed, came back to lead the army. A Christian fleet failed to stop him crossing the straits.

In the battle the young king charged the sultan's guard and was killed, and his head was shown on a spear. The crusade collapsed. It was the last large Western attempt to save Constantinople, which fell nine years later.
sum: A battle near Varna on the Black Sea coast of Bulgaria on 10 November 1444, where the Ottomans under Murad II destroyed a crusading army.
